considered  as  a  factor  in  social  or  biological

(2)  The  social  selection  of  an  individual 
for  exclusion  from  social  life  :  social  elimina 
tion. 

Social  selection  is  illustrated  well  in 
matrimony — say,  the  marriage  of  a  white  man 
to  a  negro  woman  in  New  York — since  the 
result  is  influential  biologically  as  well  as 
socially  :  socially,  because  the  children  are 
trained  by  a  woman  of  low  culture  and  are 
socially  ostracized  (social  heredity);  and 
biologically,  because  their  strain  of  negro 
blood,  by  shutting  them  up  to  negro  marriages 
(except  in  very  rare  instances),  is  continued 
and  strengthened  in  later  generation.-  (physi 
cal  heredity).  This  latter  point  is  referred  to 
elsewhere  (see  SociONOMK  FOKCKS.  3). 

The  influence  of  social  selection  on  bio 
logical  evolution  has  been  recogni/.ed  in  many 
ways  in  recent  discussion.  Wallace  calls  it 
'  selective  association  '  in  cases  in  which  it
